full_judgment:
2. It appears that the plaintiff-opposite party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1985 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong on 2.2.1985 for permission to sue as pauper for recovery of the sum of Tk. 3,09,667.00 on account of prompt dower, maintenance, value of gold ornaments, marriage clothings, furniture and other presents and the said case was dismissed for the default on 12.3.86 in the absence of both the parties for failure of the plaintiff-opposite party Shahanara Begum to show cause or to take any other step. It further appears that during pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1985 the opposite party Shahanara Begum filed on 27.1.1986 Money Suit No. 1 (FC) of 1986 in the 2nd Court of Munsif and Family Court, PS Double Moorings, Chittagong for recovery of the self-same amount of Tk. 3,09,667.00. In that suit the defendant-petitioner filed an application under section 6(2)(a) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 and after hearing by order dated 30.3.87 the plaint was rejected. The plaintiff-opposite party Shahanara Begum being aggrieved by the said order preferred Family Court Appeal No. 26 of 1987 and by judgment dated 28.4.88 the appeal was allowed and the order dated 30.3.87 rejecting the plaint was set aside. Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner obtained Rule from this Court challenging the said impugned judgment and order dated 28.4.88. 

 3. The only question raised in this Rule is that under section 27 of the Family Courts Ordinance pending suits, appeals and other proceedings relating to or arising out of any of the matters specified in section 5 (exclusively vesting jurisdiction in the Family Court) pending in the Civil Court shall continue in that Court and not in the Family Court and as such the suit filed in the Family Court by the plaintiff-opposite party during pendency of her pauper case in the Court of the Subordinate Judge was not maintainable and the Court of appeal below acted illegally in setting aside the order of the Family Court rejecting the plaint. 

 4. Mr. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner relying on the decision in the case of Suratannessa Vs. Md. Naimuddin reported in 18 DLR 37 submitted that the petition in a pauper case is the plaint of the suit and as such the case was to be continued by the plaintiff petitioner in the Court of the Subordinate Judge and that she is not entitled in law to file and maintain the suit in the Family Court for the self-same relief in view of the provision of section 27 of the Ordinance. 

 5. Mr. Mozammel Hossain, learned Advocate for the opposite party submitted that section 27 of the Ordinance was a saving provision for excluding the pending cases in the Civil Court from the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court but the same did not debar the plaintiff-opposite party to file a suit in the Family Court even during the pendency of the Miscellaneous Case for permission to sue as pauper and the case cited by the petitioner's Advocate rather helping his contention than supporting the contention of the petitioner inasmuch as it was held in that case that the date of presentation of the petition in pauper case shall be deemed to be the date of filing the plaint only for the purpose of limitation. He further submitted that there is no bar in filing two suits for the same relief in two Courts but the same will be subject to the disabilities under sections 10 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submitted that there is no provision in the Family Courts Ordinance to reject the plaint and the Court of appeal below rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the erroneous order of the Family Court rejecting the plaint. 

 6. Under section 6(2)(a) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 if the Family Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the suit, the plaint shall be returned for presenting the same to the proper Court. In this case there was no objection that Family Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the suit filed by the plaintiff opposite party in that Court. On perusal of a copy of the plaint in Money Suit. No. 1(FC) of 1986 it appears that the plaintiff claimed a sum of Tk. 80,001.00 as prompt dower and Tk. 69,666.00 as maintenance, Tk. 1,00,000.00 as value of gold ornaments and Tk. 60,000.00 as value of her personal belongings. In the pauper case also the plaintiff claimed recovery of the self-same amounts. Under section 5 of the Family Courts Ordinance claim for dower and maintenance was within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court and the claim for recovery of value of gold ornaments and personal belongings was not within the exclusive jurisdiction of that Court. Since part of the claim was within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court the suit filed by the plaintiff opposite party in the Family Court was maintainable as there was no bar in filing the suit in that Court. Assuming that the petition for permission to sue as a pauper was a plaint, that will mean that on the date of filing the suit in the Family Court there was another suit pending for the self-same claim in the Court of the Subordinate Judge. We find no bar either under the Family Courts Ordinance or under the Code of Civil. Procedure in filing two separate suits in two different Courts for the self-same relief. Of course under section 10 of the Code the subsequent suit can be stayed and under section 11 of the Code the decision in one case will be binding in the other case on the principle of res-judicata. Under the provision of section 20 of the Ordinance sections 10 and 11 of the Code shall apply in respect of a suit in the Family Court. Section 27 of the Ordinance reads as follows : 

 "27. Provisions relating to pending cases.—Notwithstanding anything contained in this Ordinance, all suits, appeals and other legal proceedings relating to, or arising out of, any of the matters specified in section 5 pending in any Court immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance shall continue in the same Court and shall be heard and disposed of by that Court as if this Ordinance had not been made". 

 From the above provisions it is clear that pending cases in any Court other than Family Court relating to and arising out of, the matters within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court shall continue in that Court and shall be heard and disposed of by that Court. There is no bar under the said provision to withdraw or discontinue a pending case from any other Court and in filing a fresh suit in the Family Court for the self-same relief. The provision is to save the pending cases in any Court other than the Family Court relating to matters within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court and not to bar a suit or a case to be filed and entertained by the Family Court for the self-same claim. 

 7. Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1985 filed by the plaintiff opposite party for permission to sue as a pauper was dismissed for default on 12.3.86 in the absence of both the parties and as such bar under the provisions of Order IX rule 9 of the Code will not apply to the plaintiff-opposite party to file a fresh suit in respect of the same cause of action. But under the provision of section 20 of the Ordinance the Code except sections 10 and 11 shall not apply to proceedings before the Family Court. So even if bar under Order IX rule 9 of the Code was applicable for filing a fresh suit in the Civil Code in view of the above provision of section 20 of the Ordinance such bar will not apply to the suit filed by the plaintiff-opposite party in the Family Court. 

 9. We, therefore, find no illegality in the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below. Moreover the pauper case was filed on 2.2.85 whereas Family Courts Ordinance, was published in the official Gazette on 30.3.85 subsequent to the filing of the case. Since the Ordinance provided for speedy disposal of cases filed with a fixed court fee of Tk. 25.00 the plaintiff-opposite party found it convenient to file the case in the Family Court and subsequently allowed the pauper case to be dismissed for default. As there is no legal bar to file and proceed with the suit filed in the Family Court, it cannot be said that the suit was not maintainable in that Court. There was no illegality on the part of the Court of appeal below resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal. We have noticed from the lower Court's record that the defendant petitioner after service of summons entered appearance on 3.6.86 fixed for ex-parte disposal of the case and obtained several adjournments for filling written statement and filed written statement on 18.11.86 and thereafter 3.1.87 was fixed for pre-trial hearing under section 10 of the Ordinance and on that date the defendant was found absent on call and 5.1.87 was fixed for ex parte disposal of the suit. The said order was however vacated on the application of the petitioner and again 5.1.87 was fixed for pre-trial hearing which was shifted to 7.1.87 when the petitioner filed the petition for rejection of the plaint and as such he is liable to pay compensatory cost to the opposite party for abusing process of the Court and unnecessarily harassing the plaintiff-opposite party by taking resort to every means to delay the disposal of the suit though Family Court has been set up under the said Ordinance for quick disposal of cases filed there. 

 11. Let the LC records be sent down at once. The trial Court is directed to dispose of the suit within 3 months from the date of receipt of the records and not to grant unnecessary adjournments as the Ordinance provides for speedy and summary disposal of the cases dispensing with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
